source: The eight classes are transcribed from CODB01Classes.xlsx, descriptions included, exactly as written there. Weapon and attachment names are normalised to the spellings used elsewhere in the app. Killstreaks are not part of a class here — they are called per map, because what is worth running depends on the ground, not the gun.
note: There is no score. A number out of 100 implied a precision that wasn't there. What each class is good and bad at is worked out from its own parts — the weapon's reach and time-to-kill from weapons.json, the perks, the attachments — against the map you pick.

presets.name: xJawz
presets.description: OG Pub-stomper who's class is set up for big streaks.

presets.name: Chabba
presets.description: He's a wanker, but a bigger flanker. Also loves shooting shit down.

presets.name: Baz
presets.description: A class for getting into the mixer, winning scraps and getting diddled from behind due to your horrible lack of awareness.

presets.name: Nuketown
presets.description: SMG and bomb proof for fully getitng involved in Nuketown.

presets.name: CQB
presets.description: A class for small maps, to help fight, streak and protect from throwables.

presets.name: Long Range
presets.description: A class for picking long range fights and staying hidden.

presets.name: Rush
presets.description: A class to fly around the map and probably lose all your gunfights with.

traits.note: Each rule fires off the build itself. Where a rule needs a number — reach, time-to-kill — the app pulls it live from weapons.json rather than repeating it here, so these lines can't drift from the weapon data.

rules.excels: Staying unseen. Off the enemy minimap even when a Spy Plane is up, and silent on foot — you can take the long way round and arrive where nobody is looking.
Getting streaks out. Every reward comes a kill early, which is the difference between a Blackbird you talk about and one you actually call in.
Winning trades you didn't start. Less flinch when you're hit first, so a fight you walked into blind is still winnable.
Surviving the clutter. Explosives and stuns are how you die on a small map, and this stops both.
Staying in the fight. The reload between two contacts is where a lot of deaths happen.
Covering ground. You get to the good spots before the people who want them.
Fitting the gun to the ground. Two attachments means you don't have to choose between seeing the target and staying off the radar.

rules.struggles: Knowing when to stop. Endless sprint mostly subsidises running into rooms you haven't cleared.
Actually saving you. In Team Deathmatch the other team has already banked the kill, and it costs the slot Ninja wants.
The Tier 1 slot. Nothing in it is pulling weight — Ghost, Hardline or Flak Jacket all do more than what's there.
The Tier 3 slot. Ninja alone is worth more than an empty one.

rules.excels: Not showing up when you shoot. No dot on their minimap, so the first kill of a hold doesn't tell the map where you are.
Long holds. More rounds before you're the one reloading in a doorway.
Back-to-back fights. The first reload is close to instant, which is the one that matters.
Room-to-room fighting. Fast to aim, fast to move, and it wins anything decided inside a doorway.

rules.struggles: Being rushed. Aim-in is slow and a miss costs you MISS_PENALTY before you can fire again.

rules.excels: Holding a line. The magazine outlasts anyone trying to push through it.
rules.struggles: Reacting. Slow to aim and slow to move — you have to be set up before the fight starts.

rules.excels: Landing a full burst at range — the whole burst hits for one trigger pull, so distance costs you nothing in accuracy.
rules.struggles: A burst that misses. There is a forced gap before the next one, and at close range that gap is the fight.

rules.excels: Picking fights before the other side can answer. WEAPON_REACH

rules.struggles: Explosives. On ground this tight the grenades find you whether you deserve it or not, and there's no Flak Jacket here.
Getting value from Flak Jacket. On a map this size you'll be shot far more often than you'll be blown up.
